Industry News: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Crunchbase

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in October, reports that OpenAI‘s annualized revenue was running well below earlier estimates sent AI-linked stocks sharply lower and prompted a fresh round of scrutiny over AI valuations.
  • It has been revealed that the limitations have been understood for some time.
  • Industry observers note that for founders, this is worth paying attention to now rather than later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in October, reports that OpenAI‘s annualized revenue was running well below earlier estimates sent AI-linked stocks sharply lower and prompted a fresh round of scrutiny over AI valuations. It also reopened a question investors have been circling for a while: Is ARR still the right way to describe an AI business?

It has been revealed that the limitations have been understood for some time. ARR was built for software companies selling predictable annual contracts, which is only part of how most AI companies make money. Through the early part of the generative AI boom, growth was steep enough that few people pressed the point. The OpenAI episode has made it harder to leave alone, partly because it demonstrated how much weight public markets now place on a single private company’s numbers.

Industry observers note that for founders, this is worth paying attention to now rather than later. A cohort of AI companies is reaching the growth-capital stage, and the questions they face in diligence are changing.

Sources indicate that ARR became standard in the mid- to late-2000s, when software moved from licence fees to recurring subscriptions. A customer signed for 12 months, revenue became predictable and annualizing it was arithmetic rather than forecasting.

Sources indicate that the first generation of post-ChatGPT companies inherited it without much examination, despite earning money in a different way. Most now run hybrid models: a subscription base with consumption charges on top, billed against API calls, tokens processed or compute used. A growing number charge per outcome. An annualized figure blends revenue a customer has committed to with revenue that depends on what they use next month.

Industry observers note that what gets presented as ARR is usually a revenue run rate: recent revenue multiplied out to an annual figure. That is a reasonable way to describe momentum, and a less reliable guide to the year ahead. The first question an investor tends to ask is what the figure actually counts.

Companies that sell partly through partners can report either the full value of those sales or only the share they keep, and the two conventions produce very different numbers for the same business. Both are legitimate, but the two are not necessarily comparable.

Take two companies both reporting a $10 million annualized run rate. In the first, most of that revenue is contracted, and comes from customers whose usage has expanded steadily over 12 months. In the second, it rests on a handful of customers whose consumption spiked in the last quarter.

These are not similar businesses. The first has demonstrated that customers keep coming back and spending more. Nothing in the headline figure tells you that.

If a single figure cannot separate those two businesses, the question is what can. The answer depends on the stage. At pre-seed and seed, the number matters. A steep trajectory can point to market demand, to customers willing to pay, and to a team beginning to crack go-to-market. A run rate isn’t generally expected to predict the year at that size.

Recent findings suggest that later you need more. What matters is the revenue behind the number: customer concentration, how much is contracted rather than consumed, how predictable that revenue is, and whether the gross margins hold as volume rises.

Retention and expansion are the centerpiece. They tell you how essential a product has become and whether it will still be in use in a few years. Churn is diagnostic in a way a growth figure never is. It can point to demand the product is not answering, pricing that does not match the value, a need that was never really recurring, or a market shallower than it first looked.

ARR has been a staple of how high-growth tech companies demonstrate momentum for such a long time that it’s not likely to disappear anytime soon.

According to recent reports, what is changing is how much weight that single number can carry on its own. Expect more investors to ask what a figure actually counts, how much of it is committed revenue, and what retention looks like by cohort. The founders who have those answers ready will tell a much more convincing story than a single number ever could.

Kenza Zayani is an early-stage investor at RTP Global, based in London. She is drawn to ambitious founders tackling the most challenging problems, with a particular interest in AI from infrastructure to applications. Zayani has built experience in venture capital across stages, and at RTP Global, she brings her multistage experience and data-driven approach to organization building with founders.

So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.
  • It has been revealed that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn.
  • Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a substantial decision to make in the next few weeks: take the organization’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm.

It has been revealed that nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a substantial decision to make in the next few weeks: take the organization’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

It has been revealed that microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman revealed the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The manufacturer expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft says the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in newly introduced hires.

According to recent reports, the worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the firm decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

Sources indicate that there is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

One of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

According to recent reports, hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more vital than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

Recent findings suggest that the jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

Sources indicate that AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI company today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual manufacturer. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software firm.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a firm.

Sources indicate that software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

Recent findings suggest that this cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

Recent findings suggest that the true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue quickly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

According to recent reports, the bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

One venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

There are three fundraising paths.

1) Think VERY major, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

It has been revealed that 2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a tech giant that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

Sources indicate that 3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

There are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

According to recent reports, other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Sources indicate that whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Substantial Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a newly introduced role, a company of their own or a year with their family.

Tech Report: Trump’s ‘assurance’ to Nvidia’s board over national security: Protection from a major source of legal danger?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of Nvidia’s board of directors voting unanimously to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his ouster, President Donald Trump effectively gave them a major reprieve from some legal liabilities, one corporate governance expert said.
  • Trump told CNBC on Monday that Nvidia’s board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” seemingly referring to a White House guarantee that the board would be exempt from liability regarding its former and current CEO’s embroilment in an international scandal.
  • It has been revealed that A White House spokesperson confirmed Trump’s role to Fortune: “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of Nvidia’s board of directors voting unanimously to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang less than two weeks after his ouster, President Donald Trump effectively gave them a major reprieve from some legal liabilities, one corporate governance expert said.

Trump told CNBC on Monday that Nvidia’s board “did ask for assurance on the national security threat,” seemingly referring to a White House guarantee that the board would be exempt from liability regarding its former and current CEO’s embroilment in an international scandal. “And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot.”.

It has been revealed that A White House spokesperson confirmed Trump’s role to Fortune: “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board. We have to protect our geniuses.”.

Huang, who cofounded the semiconductor chip giant 33 years ago, resigned earlier this month following revelations of an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence reportedly deemed a Chinese operative. Alice Huang was also an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, which is being investigated for allegedly smuggling at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips. The Nvidia CEO also faces allegations of affairs with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, and a second unnamed Nvidia employee; it is unclear which scandal prompted his resignation.

Nvidia’s board reportedly met on Sunday night, just hours after Trump made a call on social media for Huang’s reinstatement.

Ann Lipton, a law professor at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who specializes in corporate governance, said Trump’s assurances over national security were likely one of the defining factors in the board’s decision to reinstate Huang, as it granted the board a newly introduced level of legal protection.

“Once it became clear that the board was no longer going to be legally vulnerable, that’s when I think it became inevitable that this was going to play out,” Lipton told Fortune.

In a recent development, nvidia’s board had no clear succession blueprint, and Huang had up to 60 direct reports, making it difficult to check the CEO’s authority, some experts warned. In its announcement of Huang’s reinstatement, Nvidia said it would hire a chief compliance officer, which the company has never had.

In September 2003, the Securities and Exchange Commission concluded its probe into the company and filed financial reporting fraud charges against former CFO Christine B. Hoberg, claiming she had failed to report $3.3 million in expenses. The CFO paid a $672,000 settlement. In 2022, Nvidia paid the SEC $5.5 million in civil penalties over inadequate disclosures regarding how cryptocurrency mining bolstered its gaming GPU sales.

Nvidia has also previously been accused of using monopolistic tactics, including in 2021, when the Federal Trade Commission blocked the firm’s attempt to purchase chip firm Arm. Now, in addition to the Department of Justice investigating Nvidia’s knowledge of Megaspeed’s alleged chip smuggling, it is also reportedly facing an SEC probe over any accounting irregularities and inadequate disclosures over questionable chip sales in Asia.

While loose board oversight works when stock prices are high, Lipton mentioned, any legal scandal can put the board in jeopardy, which is what happened when news of Huang’s affair came to a head. Legal scandals don’t just put the company in jeopardy, but also the board personally. If the board hadn’t pushed Huang to resign earlier this month, they could have been held liable for a failure of oversight or acquiescing in securities fraud, according to Lipton.

“In that context, it may very well have seemed to the board like firing Huang and creating this internal investigation was really the only way that they could separate themselves from him,” she remarked.

While there was market pressure to rehire Huang—Nvidia’s stock fell 28% from Huang’s resignation through Friday’s market close—Trump’s assurances alleviated legal pressures put on the board, and the individuals on the board, Lipton explained.

Sources indicate that “What the board would have been vulnerable to is essentially a claim that they fail to exercise proper oversight,” she said. “You can’t make that claim if the president of the United States is assuring you that there are no legal risks, even if something were to be uncovered, even if something were to be uncovered by a future administration.”.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to Fortune’s request for comment.

Trump’s comments don’t guard Nvidia’s board from all legal risks, however. According to Jonathan Macey, a professor of corporate law, corporate finance, and securities law at Yale Law School, while board members may not face criminal legal pressure, they are still vulnerable to civil risks for corporate governance failures.

According to recent reports, board members may still be subject to lawsuits filed by shareholders, as well as congressional investigations, particularly after a Democratic midterm sweep. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer signaled on Monday prepares to probe parties involved in Huang’s reinstatement.

“Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” Schumer wrote on social media.

Trump’s comments about his role in reinstating Huang have raised speculation about the president’s plans to preemptively pardon the Nvidia CEO, but corporate governance experts agreed Trump pardoning Huang would not hold the same benefits for Nvidia’s board. A preemptive pardon—which the Trump administration has offered no public intentions of issuing—would signal that there was a nontrivial possibility of Huang being in danger of a criminal conviction, which could mount even more pressure on the board as to why they reinstated him.

“All that does is mean that this guy probably did something really awful from a director’s point of view,” Macey told Fortune. “It makes it worse.”.

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

Industry observers note that but a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

It has been revealed that the summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It reveals how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:.

According to recent reports, it also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain.".

In a recent development, A no vote would stop the whole blueprint. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis.".

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":.

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC highlighted almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

Sources indicate that the portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks.".

It has been revealed that why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

Industry observers note that the spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence shows what that requirement means on-chain.

According to recent reports, so Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

Sources indicate that for now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:.

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":.

In a recent development, the second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the strategy goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

Recent findings suggest that the Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln.

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

It has been revealed that according to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

Recent findings suggest that “So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more quickly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

“Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Industry observers note that third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Sources indicate that watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”.

As AI Takes on More Work, a Leader’s Responsibility Only Grows. Here’s Why.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, over the past few years, entrepreneurs have been living in a state of constant mobilization.
  • After several years of running this marathon, it might seem that we should finally be able to catch our breath.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

In a recent development, over the past few years, entrepreneurs have been living in a state of constant mobilization. First came the pandemic, followed by geopolitical instability, shifting markets, the emergence of artificial intelligence and a latest generation of technology-driven competitors.

After several years of running this marathon, it might seem that we should finally be able to catch our breath. Yet it is precisely now that we are beginning to realize that the pace of change is only accelerating.

Sources indicate that we have become accustomed to looking for ways to manage stress: exercise, saunas, digital detoxes and meditation. But perhaps the problem is not simply how much time we spend resting. Perhaps the pace of change itself has fundamentally shifted.

According to recent reports, the defining feature of our time is the exponential development of technology. Today, we are no longer talking simply about digitalization, but about the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. AI is ceasing to be a standalone tool and is beginning to shape the environment in which businesses operate. It accelerates analysis, automates processes, changes consumer expectations and reduces the cost of many operations.

But as opportunities grow, so does human responsibility.

In a recent development, in the past, a firm could operate for years based on a strategy chosen once and then followed consistently. Today, almost every change becomes a separate project: introducing artificial intelligence, modifying a product, restructuring sales channels or adapting to upcoming customer habits. Entrepreneurs are no longer simply making decisions; they are constantly managing change.

In a recent development, uncertainty is increasingly becoming the environment in which businesses are built. The question for every entrepreneur is whether they can make decisions and take action under such conditions.

I often say that entrepreneurship is not so much a profession as a state of mind. Education, planning and capital all help, but entrepreneurs must act with incomplete information, adapt, overcome setbacks and maintain the emotional balance required to lead others.

Recent findings suggest that this is precisely why emotional intelligence matters so much. Strong analysts can be hired, but a leader must personally learn to manage their own reactions, understand others and communicate convincingly in stressful situations.

According to recent reports, A team takes its cues from its leader. If the leader freezes, the organization slows down. If they act recklessly, it risks losing discipline. The challenge is to remain calm without becoming passive, and optimistic without ignoring risks.

Persistence is equally important: that inner drive that keeps you working until you achieve the desired result. At the same time, the tools and the route may change. It is important not to confuse persistence with stubbornness, or activity with actual progress.

It has been revealed that the paradox is that as AI takes over more routine tasks, the responsibility of leaders continues to grow. It is the human being who determines the direction of development, builds the team and assesses strategic risks. The ability to understand what is happening and adapt more rapidly is therefore becoming a key competitive advantage.

Industry observers note that A leader can only step away from the controls when there are people around them capable of taking over. This makes one of the most important resources available to any leader the ability to build a strong team, establish trust with partners and delegate authority.

But there is a question that I believe is far more crucial than efficiency.

We talk far too often about how to outperform competitors, increase market capitalization or scale a business. Almost never do we ask ourselves a different question: What is the ultimate purpose of being human?

Industry observers note that you can defeat your competitors, build the largest company and achieve extraordinary results. Yet none of these things guarantees what matters most: a happy life.

Industry observers note that most people define their goals in terms of achievements. Almost nobody notes: My primary goal is to build the happiest possible life for myself. Yet this is precisely the goal that determines the value of all other achievements!

It has been revealed that inner exhaustion is not always simply a matter of how much work we do. If the lifestyle we have chosen consistently leads to it, we should ask ourselves what goals we are pursuing. Perhaps something needs to change.

According to recent reports, so perhaps the most useful advice for entrepreneurs today is surprisingly simple: Start by understanding yourself. Understand your genuine emotional needs, strengths, natural abilities and limitations. Do not try to become someone you are not. Do not build a career that goes against your own nature.

According to recent reports, people generally enjoy doing things they are good at. And they tend to become good at things they genuinely enjoy doing. When these two things coincide, the likelihood of success increases significantly.

This applies beyond business. Even philanthropy, traditionally regarded as an exclusively altruistic activity, naturally benefits the person who gives as well. The opportunity to share knowledge, help others and see the results of one’s actions all generate positive emotions. There is nothing wrong with that. It is simply human nature.

In general, many things become easier to understand when viewed through the lens of biology rather than conventional abstractions. Our emotions, motivation and sense of fulfillment have a very real physiological basis. Relationships with other people, meaningful work, the environment in which we live, our health and our ability to take pleasure in our own achievements — these are the elements that combine to create a sense of well-being.

Sources indicate that happiness, therefore, is neither a matter of luck nor a state of constant euphoria. It is a dynamic balance between the emotions a person genuinely needs and the states they experience at any given moment. This balance cannot be found once and preserved forever. It must be maintained continuously, with adjustments to our lives as the world around us changes.

And perhaps this is one of the greatest challenges of the age of artificial intelligence.

It has been revealed that machines may become increasingly capable of analyzing data, writing code, creating content, automating processes and helping us make decisions. But help with a decision is not the same as responsibility for it. The question of why we are in business and what kind of life we want to live remains ours to answer.

That is why a leader’s true competitive advantage lies not only in the ability to use AI, but also in the ability to remain the author of their own life.

Technology may change the rules of the game many times over. The pace of change may accelerate, and artificial intelligence may take over a significant share of intellectual work. But responsibility for our own decisions, our own happiness and our own path will remain with us.

And perhaps this is the most valuable skill a leader can possess today: the ability to maintain inner strength and remain the author of their own life, even as the world around them changes faster than ever before.

Over the past few years, entrepreneurs have been living in a state of constant mobilization. First came the pandemic, followed by geopolitical instability, shifting markets, the emergence of artificial intelligence and a new generation of technology-driven competitors.

After several years of running this marathon, it might seem that we should finally be able to catch our breath. Yet it is precisely now that we are beginning to realize that the pace of change is only accelerating.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Latest Yorkers’ doors.
  • Recent findings suggest that the legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:51 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:51 pm.

Amazon and New York City are fighting again.

The Seattle tech giant is threatening to move its delivery operations out of the city over a proposed law that would require it to directly employ the drivers who bring packages to Latest Yorkers’ doors. It’s also asking its customers to help fight the bill.

Recent findings suggest that the legislation, known as the Delivery Protection Act or Intro 518, would apply to companies that run last-mile delivery facilities in the city. Amazon is the main target, but FedEx and several regional couriers would also be covered.

Companies would need a license from the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which would also investigate complaints. The bill was introduced in February.

According to recent reports, on Thursday, Amazon began showing New York City customers pop-up messages and a homepage banner that reads, “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The notices link to a form and a pre-written letter customers can send to their council members to oppose the bill, Bloomberg reported. Amazon pointed GeekWire to a study by consulting firm AKRF estimating the bill would raise consumer costs by $409 to $664 a year, but didn’t detail how it arrived at the per-order figure.

Sources indicate that in a blog post, Amazon said it relies on a network of small delivery businesses in the city. “If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city,” the company wrote. “That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in Upcoming York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.”.

Amazon launched its Delivery Service Partners program in 2018, letting entrepreneurs start their own companies to deliver Amazon packages in Amazon-branded vans and uniforms. The companies hire their own drivers, while Amazon pays them to deliver and offers discounts on vehicles, fuel and insurance. The model lets Amazon expand its delivery network without directly employing drivers.

It has been revealed that in a statement to GeekWire, Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel noted the bill “as written” would threaten more than 40 small delivery businesses the company works with in the city and the more than 5,000 Upcoming Yorkers they employ. More than 2,000 Amazon employees also work at its delivery facilities in the city, the company said.

According to recent reports, “We’re hopeful this bill doesn’t pass as written,” Nantel said. “But so far, key City Council members seem uninterested in learning about our delivery operations.” Amazon said neither Council Member Tiffany Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, nor Mayor Zohran Mamdani has accepted its offer to visit a delivery facility. The company also said customers sent about 20,000 emails to council members within six hours of the campaign’s launch Thursday morning.

The standoff echoes Amazon’s 2019 reversal on its second headquarters. That February, the tech giant abruptly canceled plans to build a 25,000-person “HQ2” office in Long Island City, Queens, after more than a year of competition among cities to host it. Amazon blamed “a number of state and local politicians” who opposed the project, which drew fierce criticism over roughly $3 billion in government incentives.

Recent findings suggest that amazon stuck with its aims for Arlington, Va., and Nashville and didn’t reopen its search. Polls at the time showed most Upcoming Yorkers supported the deal, but Queens officials, labor leaders and activists fought it. State Sen. Michael Gianaris, who led the opposition, accused Amazon of trying to shake down governments to get its way.

It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise Fresh Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections.We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.If… https://t.co/UWXVTJhRL6.

City leaders backing the delivery bill see a familiar pattern. “Amazon is once again making spurious attacks against this commonsense legislation that would make workers and our streets safer,” said Cabán, the bill’s sponsor, who called Amazon’s warning a “dishonest scare tactic.”.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin questioned Amazon’s cost claims in a post on X.

“It defies logic that Amazon, a $3 trillion corporation, would raise New Yorkers’ cost of living if it’s forced to adhere to basic regulations and worker protections,” she wrote, adding that the council is “crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs.”.

Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon’s subcontractor model “leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets,” CNBC reported.

Supporters, including the Teamsters union, which has sought to organize Amazon drivers and warehouse workers, say the bill would make the work safer and make it harder for Amazon to distance itself from driver injuries.

Amazon disputes that the bill would improve safety. The tech giant remarked it has invested more than $2.5 billion in driver safety since 2019, that the serious crash rate for its drivers in Newly introduced York City fell 35.7% from 2024 to 2025, and that drivers there have averaged nearly $24 an hour since January 2025, with required health coverage and paid time off.

Meanwhile, business groups have run ads against the bill and warned they may sue the city if it passes, according to CNBC. The measure is awaiting review by Menin.

According to recent reports, XRP’s return below the psychologically vital $1 level hasn’t convinced every investor that it is time to buy the dip. Despite believing the payments-based token could eventually climb to a staggering $10, one trader is holding back. His cautious stance raises an interesting question: if XRP has such massive upside potential, why is he waiting on the sidelines?

In a November 19 post on X, crypto trader VirtualBacon identified the $1 price level as a potential bottoming zone for XRP in the current market cycle. The analyst suggested that the cryptocurrency may be approaching the lower end of its correction, even as selling pressure continues to weigh on its price.

“For me, $1 is roughly the bottom area for this cycle,” he stated.

While he described the $1 mark as the approximate bottoming zone for XRP during the ongoing cycle, he did not suggest that a definitive price floor had already been established.

His hesitation stems from the belief that investors will still have plenty of opportunities to accumulate alternative cryptocurrencies even after the broader market begins recovering. In his view, many altcoins could remain relatively cheap early in the next market rebound, meaning investors don’t necessarily need to rush into XRP before its downtrend runs its course.

“I’m not buying it yet,” he explained, making it clear that he would rather wait for a more favorable entry point than rush into the market.

XRP was trading at $0.9647 at the time of publication, down 2.3% over the previous 24 hours. The latest pullback followed a brief recovery to $1 on November 18, 2026, which proved short-lived as investors took profits, pushing the token back below the key psychological threshold.

Although VirtualBacon is not ready to accumulate XRP at current prices, he remains optimistic about its longer-term potential. The pundit believes the cryptocurrency could eventually reach $10, although he sees limited room for significant gains beyond that valuation.

Sources indicate that A rally to $10 would represent a major milestone for XRP, pushing its market capitalization to approximately $635 billion based on a circulating supply of 63.52 billion tokens. This would place the cryptocurrency among the largest digital assets by market value and require its valuation to grow more than tenfold from current levels.

Recent findings suggest that the projected price target also highlights the scale of growth XRP would need. At $10 per token, its fully diluted valuation, calculated using the maximum supply of 100 billion XRP, would reach approximately $1 trillion.

However, reaching such a valuation would require sustained demand, increased market participation, and significant capital flowing into the cryptocurrency. Notably, while VirtualBacon considers $10 achievable over the longer term, his outlook suggests that he sees this level as a more realistic upper target rather than expecting XRP to deliver substantially higher gains.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq tomorrow with a growth story that’s unlike any I’ve seen in close to three decades working in Silicon Valley: The company notes revenue reached $17 billion in Q3, less than four years after Claude rolled out with zero.

The San Francisco-based company also presents a stark contrast to the more common theme in recent years of venture-backed companies staying private longer: Anthropic is less than six years old as it goes public in a potentially record-setting listing.

Those metrics are impressive, but there are other numbers in its S-1 I keep circling, too, like the nearly $900 billion in compute purchase and lease commitments.

Sources indicate that I’ve worked in Silicon Valley through the dot-com boom and bust, the rise of SaaS, social media, unicorn and decacorn startups and now, AI. Anthropic’s extraordinary rise and entrance onto the public markets marks a new technology era — one with enormous growth and potential, but also tremendous costs, risks and unknowns.

OpenAI’s seminal success was the launch of chatbots in 2022 — within two months, ChatGPT reached 100 million users and in less than four years, OpenAI had a billion monthly active users.

By contrast, Anthropic’s breakout was the success of Claude Code, debuted just last year. Already, Anthropic claims 11,900 companies use the product, spending $100,000 or more trailing 12 months, up 12x from a year ago. In its S-1, the firm says that marks the fastest enterprise adoption for any company on record.

Anthropic’s IPO could value it at $1.4 trillion and raise $88.5 billion via the IPO and concurrent private placement. As it becomes public, I’ll be watching closely to see if the company can keep turning demand for Claude and Claude Code into a durable business while building out the astounding amount of compute it says it needs and managing the many risks that surround its technology.

Here are some of the other key details and figures that caught my eye ahead of Anthropic’s first day on the public markets:.

Anthropic got to where it is now through a fast sequence of funding rounds, from its Jaan Tallinn-led Series A in 2021 to its Series H in May of this year that valued the company at $965 billion.

Other lead investors over its many funding rounds include Google, Amazon, Spark Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Coatue and Sequoia Capital, all of whom are slated to be among the winners when it goes public tomorrow.

In a recent development, the AI era has the potential to generate massive amounts of latest wealth and unlock life-changing technological advances. But it also comes with huge risks. Anthropic’s S-1 captures that tension.

The opportunity the tech giant describes extends far beyond coding and software. It claims its focus in 2027 will be AI agents for knowledge work and scientific discovery. It also points to potential gains in biology and rare-disease research, economic growth, wider access to health care and improved government services. The S-1 cites the World Health Organization’s estimate that 4.6 billion people lack access to basic health services.

That promise comes with a competitive risk for its customers, too: Companies may worry that data they share with AI providers could help train models that compete with their products, or that more capable models could erode parts of their existing businesses.

Anthropic’s S-1 also flags risks ranging from cyber and biological attacks to unpredictable model behavior, authoritarian surveillance and economic disruption.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic’s public-benefit structure is meant to balance those competing pressures. As a public benefit corporation, the company says it must weigh commercial success against the public good. Its founders, employees and Long-Term Benefit Trust share in governance; the trust has no financial stake and weighs impacts on national security, economics, global health and science. Anthropic points to its launch of Mythos as an example of that balance.

As Anthropic debuts tomorrow, I’ll be watching how well it balances AI’s promise with the risks its own filing lays out.

  • In a recent development, as per the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investment firm Roundhill has suddenly terminated intends to launch two fresh XRP- and Solana (SOL)-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

This decision comes after over a year of regulatory filings and multiple delays.

In a recent development, as per the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings on Nov. 18, Roundhill has officially withdrawn looks to launch the Roundhill XRP Covered Call Strategy ETF and Roundhill Solana Covered Call Strategy ETF.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, it submitted the applications for these two funds on Oct. 17, 2025. Therefore, these two funds had been awaiting launch for over 13 months.

As per the latest regulatory filings, Roundhill has been consistently delaying the effective dates for these two funds.

However, instead of launching them, the investment firm has decided to drop both products.

In its requests to withdraw the filings for these funds, Roundhill revealed that it "has no further intention to pursue effectiveness of the Fund." The firm noted that it had not sold any shares under the registrations for these two funds.

Intriguingly, Roundhill failed to elaborate on the sudden decision to axe its looks to launch these two ETFs.

Roundhill was planning to launch income-generating XRP and Solana ETFs using a covered call strategy. In such a strategy, investors sell options to earn premiums while also maintaining exposure to the price movements of XRP and Solana.

It has been revealed that unlike spot-based ETFs, these funds would not have held the cryptocurrencies directly. Instead, they would have used options written against existing cryptocurrency ETFs.

According to recent reports, A covered call strategy can be useful for generating regular income. However, it can also cap profits during strong market rallies.

It has been revealed that notably, there has been relatively low demand for income-generating cryptocurrency investment products. This raises concerns about investors' interest in these ETFs.

Surprisingly, this decision came amid substantial net inflows into spot-based XRP and Solana ETFs.

In a recent development, U.S. spot XRP and Solana ETFs recorded net inflows of roughly $969 million between May and October 2026, according to data from SoSoValue.

Overall, these spot ETFs held around $3.26 billion in assets under management as of the end of October.

Breaking: An SEO Expert’s 3 Tactics for Getting Your Business Found Beyond Google

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Entrepreneur

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • Industry observers note that for years, getting found online meant getting found on Google.
  • But today, someone might discover a business through ChatGPT, a LinkedIn post or a recommendation from someone they trust, without ever typing a query into Google.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Industry observers note that for years, getting found online meant getting found on Google. Businesses researched keywords, optimized their websites and built backlinks to attract potential customers.

Those things still matter. But today, someone might discover a business through ChatGPT, a LinkedIn post or a recommendation from someone they trust, without ever typing a query into Google.

As an AI and SEO specialist running Create & Grow, a digital marketing agency, I’ve learned that many of the principles behind effective SEO work just as well beyond search engines. You need to understand what people are looking for, give them a reason to pay attention and build enough authority for them to trust you.

Here’s how I’ve applied those principles to client campaigns and my own business.

Keyword research tells you what people search for, but it doesn’t always reveal how they describe their problems.

According to Salesforce’s State of the Connected Customer report, 73% of customers expect companies to understand their unique needs and expectations. To do that, businesses need to listen to customers, not just study search volumes.

I saw this firsthand while working with a client in the invoicing software industry.

Instead of relying exclusively on keyword tools, we analyzed the client’s support tickets, sales calls, live chats, customer reviews and internal search data. We wanted to understand how business owners described the problems that made them look for invoicing software in the first place.

They weren’t necessarily using technical phrases like “accounts receivable automation.” They talked about chasing late payments, making mistakes on invoices, wasting hours on repetitive tasks and struggling to predict cash flow.

That distinction shaped our strategy. Rather than promoting the software through generic accounting terminology, we focused on connecting the client’s brand to the specific problems its customers wanted to solve.

We built those associations through digital PR, guest articles, LinkedIn posts, company page optimization and relevant niche edits on third-party websites. We also prioritized branded links and mentions instead of focusing exclusively on keyword-rich backlinks.

It has been revealed that our outreach campaign generated a mix of dofollow and nofollow backlinks, as well as unlinked brand mentions. Our goal wasn’t simply to earn backlinks. We wanted the client’s brand to appear consistently in conversations about the problems its software addressed.

This matters beyond traditional search. Someone might ask ChatGPT, “What software can help me stop chasing unpaid invoices?” When credible websites repeatedly connect a brand with that problem, AI systems have more relevant context about what the company offers.

That doesn’t guarantee a recommendation, but it makes the brand’s positioning clearer to both AI tools and potential customers.

Recent findings suggest that we applied the same thinking to the client’s website. We created customer case studies showing how the invoicing software solved real problems and made pricing publicly available so potential buyers could evaluate the product more easily. Both changes also made commercially useful information accessible to AI search tools.

According to recent reports, after six months, the client’s organic traffic increased by almost 25%, ranking keywords grew by 31%, and keywords in Google’s Top 10 increased by 39%. Most importantly, organic demo requests rose by 44%.

According to recent reports, those results came from our combined SEO and brand-building efforts, not one isolated tactic. We also deliberately prioritized commercial intent over traffic volume. As AI-generated answers increasingly satisfy informational searches, attracting people actively evaluating invoicing solutions matters more than ranking for every broad accounting question.

The same principle applies when you’re trying to get someone else’s attention. Before asking for anything, understand what that person might actually find valuable.

I put this into practice recently when I wanted to publish guest articles on a few high-authority websites.

Most guest-post outreach starts with a predictable request: “Do you accept guest contributions?” I wanted my message to stand out by showing editors exactly what they could gain from working with me.

In a recent development, so I researched relevant websites and contacted their editors and marketing managers with examples of articles I’d already published. These weren’t generic pieces that anyone could produce with an AI writing tool. They combined firsthand experience from real SEO campaigns, original insights, practical examples, research and relevant statistics.

I also made sure the articles were properly optimized for search, but the real selling point was the value they delivered to readers.

Then I showed the results. I included evidence of the organic traffic those articles attracted, the keywords they ranked for on Google and the citations and brand mentions they earned in AI-generated answers.

In other words, I wasn’t asking editors to imagine what I could deliver. I was showing them a finished example of the quality, expertise and measurable value I could bring to their websites.

Only then did I make my offer: “Would you like me to create something like this for your website, for free?”.

That’s a very different proposition from asking someone for a backlink or a guest-post opportunity. The editor gets a thoroughly researched, experience-driven article that can attract relevant visitors and strengthen the website’s authority. I get an opportunity to demonstrate my expertise to a new audience.

To reach people outside my existing network, I used LinkedIn Premium All-in-One, which includes InMail messaging. I didn’t need all 30 monthly InMail credits. Roughly 10 carefully targeted messages generated three client inquiries and one paying customer.

Industry observers note that some recipients became interested in my SEO consulting, content strategy and outreach services after seeing the work I could do. One tech giant ultimately hired me to improve its outreach process and develop stronger pitches.

It has been revealed that what’s interesting is that I hadn’t approached these people to sell SEO services. I led with proof of what I could create for them, made an offer that was genuinely useful and let the business conversation develop naturally.

It has been revealed that that’s why I prefer carefully researched outreach over sending hundreds of generic messages. The objective isn’t to contact as many people as possible. It’s to make your offer so relevant and valuable that the recipient has a compelling reason to respond.

In a recent development, one well-researched message can open a door. But consistently useful content can make people familiar with your work long before you ever contact them.

Industry observers note that that’s why I treat LinkedIn content planning much like SEO research. Before publishing, I study competing digital marketing agencies: their websites, LinkedIn posts and how they position their expertise. I look at which topics generate engagement, what questions their audiences ask and where their content leaves room for a better answer.

Sources indicate that I use those insights to plan content for my personal LinkedIn profile. Some posts share practical lessons about SEO, AI search and digital marketing, often drawn from my own campaigns. Others are deliberately more relaxed and humorous.

The professional posts show people how I solve problems. The humorous ones make my content more relatable and give people another reason to engage. I don’t expect every post to generate a lead, and I certainly don’t want every post to read like a sales pitch.

Instead, I want people to recognize my work over time. And that has become a reliable source of conversations and client opportunities.

According to recent reports, some people reach out through LinkedIn messages after reading my posts. Others start conversations in the comments. I’ve also met people at conferences who tell me they’ve followed my content for years. We might talk about SEO, exchange ideas and stay in touch. Sometimes, months later, they contact me about a project and become clients.

By then, I don’t need to start by explaining who I am or convincing them that I understand SEO. They’ve already seen how I think, what I know and the results I share.

In a recent development, that matters because B2B buyers often develop preferences before contacting a provider. According to 6sense‘s 2025 B2B Buyer Experience Report, in 77% of B2B purchases studied, buyers ended up choosing the firm they already preferred before their first sales conversation.

My experience illustrates why that matters in practice: Someone who has followed your work for a long time may already trust your expertise when they finally need your services.

It has been revealed that the next step is making sure that first interaction doesn’t become the last. On LinkedIn, that might mean giving readers a reason to follow your personal profile or manufacturer page. Outside LinkedIn, an email newsletter can help you stay connected with website visitors. You could even build a private Slack community where people in your industry exchange ideas, ask questions and learn from one another.

Sources indicate that whatever channel you choose, the principle is the same: Offer enough value that people want to stay connected. Then keep showing up with content worth their attention.

SEO taught me to understand what customers need, pay attention to the competition and build authority through useful content. Those principles now help me get discovered through AI tools, LinkedIn and relationships that start well before a sales conversation.

You don’t need to abandon Google or be active on every platform. Start by speaking your customers’ language, approaching latest contacts with something valuable and creating content that gives people a reason to keep following your work.

If you’re ready to make your business easier to find and harder to forget, LinkedIn’s Small Business Playbook offers practical ways to build your brand, grow your network and find customers. You can also explore LinkedIn’s tools for small businesses to see which ones fit your strategy.

Getting discovered creates the opportunity. Being remembered and trusted is what turns that opportunity into business.

Industry observers note that for years, getting found online meant getting found on Google. Businesses researched keywords, optimized their websites and built backlinks to attract potential customers.

Those things still matter. But today, someone might discover a business through ChatGPT, a LinkedIn post or a recommendation from someone they trust, without ever typing a query into Google.

Recent findings suggest that as an AI and SEO specialist running Create & Grow, a digital marketing agency, I’ve learned that many of the principles behind effective SEO work just as well beyond search engines. You need to understand what people are looking for, give them a reason to pay attention and build enough authority for them to trust you.

As FEMA pushes recovery onto states, a Miami startup pitches an AI case manager for disaster survivors

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When the Palisades fire tore through his Los Angeles neighborhood in January 2025, Jonathon Nostrant’s house was damaged but still standing.
  • Industry observers note that the fire was only the first ordeal.
  • Industry observers note that insurance was already a sore subject in the Palisades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the Palisades fire tore through his Los Angeles neighborhood in January 2025, Jonathon Nostrant’s house was damaged but still standing. Many of his neighbors’ homes were destroyed.

Industry observers note that the fire was only the first ordeal. Next, Nostrant encountered a tangle of federal, state, and local assistance programs, each with its own forms, eligibility rules, and deadlines. Survivors with insurance must also report their payouts to every agency they apply to, because FEMA cannot pay for losses an insurer already covers.

Industry observers note that insurance was already a sore subject in the Palisades. A year before the fire, State Farm dropped roughly 1,600 policies in the neighborhood, Fortune reported as the fire burned.

“Our insurance was fighting with us,” Nostrant noted in an interview, describing his own claim.

That experience led to AidFinder, a Miami-based startup Nostrant cofounded that uses AI to match disaster survivors with programs they may qualify for, explain eligibility rules, and prepare applications. Survivors review everything before submission. The intended customers, though, are states, which would offer the platform to residents under their own banner.

Recent findings suggest that for now, it is a pitch. AidFinder hasn’t signed its first state customer, and survivors have yet to use the platform, Refresh Miami reported on Nov. 17. Nostrant told the outlet the company is in talks with 30 states, including Florida, and that Craig Fugate, who ran FEMA under President Barack Obama, has accepted a seat on its board.

Nostrant has spent much of his career teaching machines to listen. In 2008, as a student at the University of Southern California, he debuted Moshi, a voice-activated alarm clock that responded to spoken commands and, in hindsight, foreshadowed Siri.

Industry observers note that he later founded Ivee, an early AI-powered home assistant that let customers control connected devices by voice. AidFinder applies the same idea to a far messier problem: turning a survivor’s account of what happened into the right applications for the right agencies.

The pitch arrives as Washington pushes more of the recovery burden onto states. FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton has told state emergency managers to prepare to handle more of the work themselves, and states have faced unusually long waits for federal disaster declarations.

Recounting Hamilton’s remarks at a National Emergency Management Association gathering, Nostrant described the federal message this way: “We want to empower the states, and we want to help empower the local counties and cities to be equipped, not just to respond to the disaster but help people recover.”.

In a recent development, aidFinder’s answer is a branded front door. “We’re giving the state the ability to launch a landing page that’s powered by AidFinder,” Nostrant mentioned, describing how residents would be matched with recovery programs.

Sources indicate that whatever tools states adopt, recovery paperwork starts with evidence. FEMA advises survivors to photograph or film damage inside and outside their homes before cleanup and to list damaged belongings, records that support both an insurance claim and a federal aid application.

Recent findings suggest that aidFinder is built around the same principle. Its platform lets residents store identification, tax records, and photos of their homes in a secure digital vault before disaster strikes. The question now is whether a state will pay to offer it.

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 6:33 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 6:33 pm.

Redmond, Wash.-based RBC Signals has announced a $10 million strategic growth investment aimed at accelerating the organization’s expansion into government satellite data services and the commercialization of emerging space technologies.

RBC Signals supports satellite operators by arranging access to a global network of ground stations, including its own assets and antenna facilities operated by partners.

According to recent reports, in August, for example, Blue Origin and RBC Signals confirmed a partnership to build out the ground infrastructure for Blue Origin’s Quartz communications network. RBC Signals is also a provider for the U.S. Space Force’s Joint Antenna Marketplace.

Recent findings suggest that the newly unveiled investment was led by Washington Harbour Partners, a private investment firm based in Washington, D.C. The firm ranked sixth among all defense technology investors in the Silicon Valley Defense Group’s 2026 NatSec100 Report.

“Our vision has always been to build a global, secure network of networks that makes space connectivity more accessible, flexible and reliable,” Ron Faith, RBC Signals’ president and CEO, noted today in a news release.

It has been revealed that “By bringing together infrastructure, partners and emerging technologies, we’re creating a dual-use platform that can evolve alongside the needs of the national defense and the commercial space industry,” Faith remarked. “This investment from Washington Harbour Partners will help us accelerate that vision by expanding our government services business and bringing emerging capabilities such as higher frequency bands, optical connectivity, intersatellite links and space domain awareness to market.”.

Sources indicate that mina Faltas, founder and CEO of Washington Harbour Partners, highlighted RBC Signals’ role in addressing the growing demand for space connectivity. “We see tremendous potential in the manufacturer’s ability to deliver mission-critical capabilities, and we’re excited to support the team as they enter this next phase of growth,” Faltas said.

Industry observers note that ripple's RLUSD stablecoin led the daily ranking of stablecoin inflows into decentralized finance (DeFi), according to Token Terminal data that RWA Foundation shared on X. The DeFi total value locked (TVL) of Ripple's stablecoin grew by $22.3 million over 24 hours, and Tether added $21.6 million. RWA Foundation titled its chart "Ripple led stablecoin DeFi growth.".

Sources indicate that paxos, Open Standard and Societe Generale followed with $7.8 million, $4 million and $1.2 million, respectively. World Liberty, United Stables, MetaMask, Tori and Liquity each added less than $700,000 over the same period.

According to recent reports, about $2.8 billion worth of RLUSD is in circulation, compared with about $180 billion worth of Tether's USDT. Tether's stablecoin is still more than 60 times bigger than RLUSD.

Ripple introduced RLUSD in December 2024. In mid-September 2026, RLUSD supply passed $2.44 billion, and about $1.38 billion of it was on Ethereum. About $1.05 billion was on the XRP Ledger, Ripple's home network. On Ethereum, the stablecoin is used in DeFi pools on Aave V3, Curve and Morpho.

RLUSD is issued by Standard Custody & Trust under the supervision of the Upcoming York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS), and its reserves are held at custodian bank BNY. In the fall, RLUSD received a Moody's rating and was listed on Coinbase and Robinhood, and Ripple received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch Ripple National Trust Bank.

Ripple has also integrated RLUSD with payment providers Arf, Convera and Cross River Bank, and the stablecoin is now used in dollar settlements between companies.

Industry observers note that in a CNBC interview on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse called blockchain-based transactions "a wave of emerging technology." "I think 10 years from now you'll see blockchain implemented across our financial infrastructure," he stated.

The right choice still depends on the recipient. The most meaningful gift shows that you have noticed the person behind the business.

Here are the 10 best gifts for entrepreneurs.

Square Terminal: For the business owner ready to simplify checkout.

Square Terminal combines sales, card payments and receipt-printing in one device. It’s a practical gift candidate for a store owner who wants to bundle those tasks together. Its built-in battery also allows cordless use around the business rather than keeping every transaction tied to one spot. Before ordering, ask if the recipient wants to use Square and if this terminal fits their existing setup. This product is presently over 10% off, making the final price $265.

According to recent reports, this Kindle Paperwhite has a seven-inch glare-free display, 16GB of storage and battery life of up to 12 weeks. For an entrepreneur, this gift could allow them to read a biography on a flight, return to a novel after closing the shop or finally start the book a friend recommended. Its appeal is especially clear for someone who already reads digitally but would appreciate a separate reading device. Think twice before buying if the person is devoted to paper books or has never expressed an interest in e-readers. This Kindle is $70 off for Black Friday, making it $130 total.

reMarkable Paper Pro bundle with Marker Plus and black leather Book Folio: For the handwritten thinker.

Some entrepreneurs think best by writing things out. They sketch a initiative or rewrite a sentence until the argument becomes clear. The reMarkable Paper Pro is aimed at that style of work, with an 11.8-inch color display and adjustable reading light. It is a color e-ink paper tablet that doubles as a digital notebook for writing and drawing. The requested package includes the Marker Plus pen and black leather Book Folio. As a gift, it makes the most sense for someone whose working day already involves handwritten notes, like a founder mapping a new service. This package is $100 off for Black Friday, making the final price about $700.

Industry observers note that bose QuietComfort headphones offer active noise cancellation, a built-in microphone and up to 24 hours of playback. That makes them a thoughtful choice for someone who regularly works around other people. The headphones also allow the recipient to use them for music or listening to podcasts or e-books during time off. Make sure to consider whether the recipient mentioned wanting over-ear headphones and if they already wear a pair throughout the day. Only some colors have the Black Friday discount, which is 53%, or $190 off, for a final price of $169.

This is a useful device for a small shop owner who has mentioned that their labeling process needs improvement. It’s also compact and is 25% off for Black Friday, for a final price of $43.

Their laptop battery runs out of charge just as a client meeting begins, and their phone is nearly dead too. A business owner who works across shared spaces and cafes could find a portable charger to be a thoughtful gift. This charger is a strong gift for a consultant or founder who regularly carries several devices. A Black Friday deal brings the price of this charger below $100, at 32% off, which is a 90-day low price. It costs about $91.

Shure SM7B dynamic vocal microphone: For the owner building a podcast.

It has been revealed that this gift is for a business owner who records interviews, lessons or a podcast. The Shure SM7B is a dynamic vocal microphone designed for uses including podcasting, broadcast and recording. Its pickup pattern focuses on sound in front of the microphone. The SM7B uses an XLR connection rather than a direct USB connection; the XLR is better for sound quality. The microphone is $70 off for Black Friday, bringing its price to $369 at the time of writing.

Apple Magic Mouse with USB-C: For the Apple user who wants a clean-looking accessory.

Apple’s Magic Mouse is wireless and rechargeable. Its Multi-Touch surface supports gestures such as scrolling through documents and swiping between web pages. The USB-C version includes a charging cable, and Apple indicates its battery can last about a month or more between charges. This is a good gift for an entrepreneur who already likes Apple’s mouse design. The clean accessory is a safe option if the recipient right now uses a Magic Mouse and wants another for a second workspace. The white color is on sale for $20 off this Black Friday, making its price about $60.

Soundcore P30i noise-cancelling earbuds: For an affordable, useful everyday gift.

Sources indicate that the Soundcore P30i earbuds offer noise cancellation and a charging case that doubles as a phone stand. The product listing also advertises up to 45 hours of total playback. The phone-stand feature adds a small practical touch. Their size makes them a reasonable candidate for someone who prefers carrying earbuds rather than over-ear headphones. They are perfect for listening during a commute. The earbuds were originally listed for about $50 but are more than 50% off for Black Friday, bringing the price down to $24.

Soundcore Select 4 Go Bluetooth speaker: For making the workday a little more enjoyable.

It is the ideal gift for an entrepreneur who likes having music nearby as they move between different working spaces. A Black Friday deal slashes the price to a 365-day low, making it $20 when it was originally $35.
